ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the founder, foundation council members, and any disclosed beneficiary against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Restrictive Measures List, and Panama's 'Lista Consolidada' (Consolidated List) issued by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF). Enhanced Due Diligence applies to any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) whether domestic or foreign, including family members and close associates. The Resident Agent must collect and retain evidence of screening and update the RPAB beneficial ownership information within 30 days of any change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicio de Reserva y Consulta de Nombres en Línea (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All foundation and corporation names must be submitted in the Spanish language or in the exact Latin-script transliteration of a foreign name. The name must be unique and not be confusingly similar to any existing registered entity. Diacritical marks and accents are recognized but must match the exact spelling in the registry database. The name shall not contain any word or phrase that implies governmental sponsorship, patronage, or official capacity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or its Resident Agent may, within fifteen (15) working days of the notification of rejection, file a written 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá. The petition must state the factual and legal grounds for reversal and attach a revised legal name if a minor amendment can cure the objection. If the Director General denies the reconsideration, the applicant may appeal within thirty (30) days to the Sala Tercera of the Superma Corte de Justicia (Contencioso-Administrativo) for judicial review. During the appeal, the proposed name may not be used or legalized in any commercial documentation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the statutory registered office of the Panamanian Private Interest Foundation; a licensed Resident Agent may provide a registered office address. However, a purely virtual address is not permissible for the underlying delivery-only cloud kitchen operations. The ghost kitchen business must maintain a physical food-preparation facility and relevant commercial licenses in each market where ISIC 5610 activities are performed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Probability of an unannounced physical inspection of the Panamanian registered office is estimated at 5% over the first three operational years based on the foundation's limited physical presence and the regulator's typical inspection priorities. For any ghost kitchen facility located within Panamanian territory, the physical inspection likelihood rises to 100% upon issuance of the food-safety operating permit, but such facility is not expected to be located in Panama.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Regime), as amended, Arts. 1-32; registered under the Mercantile/Foundation Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter) and Reglamento (Regulations), in notarized Spanish form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum initial endowment is required; a nominal initial endowment of USD 100 is recommended and must be evidenced by a notarized certificate. No escrow account is required, but the endowment must be fully available for the foundation's stated objects.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned initial Foundation Council members, acting at the first meeting of the Private Interest Foundation, hereby resolve as follows: (1) the initial endowment of USD 100 is acknowledged and deemed fully contributed; (2) the registered address of the foundation is established at the office of the registered agent in Panama City; (3) the Foundation Charter and Regulations are ratified, including the object to operate delivery-only cloud kitchen brands; (4) the initial Foundation Council, officers, and, where required, Protector are appointed with full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and secure licenses; (5) the registered agent is instructed to file the foundation record and pursue all operational permits. Approved by unanimous written consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Pre-Formation Documentary Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Reservation Portal / Customer Service Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search application to verify that the proposed foundation name is not registered, and reserve the name. Simultaneously, instruct local counsel to prepare the Foundation Charter and Regulations in Spanish, ensuring that the ghost kitchen/virtual brand operation is included as a permitted foundation object.
required_dossiers: Passport or QES (Qualified Electronic Signature) of the founder
Power of attorney to the Panamanian legal representative, if applicable
Name search and reservation application form
Brief description of the foundation's commercial purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected due to similarity, submit an alternative name reservation; if the application is queried, correct the applicant data or identify documentation within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de Panamá / Panamanian Law Firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Foundation Charter and Regulations before a Panamanian notary. The Charter must name the foundation, identify the founder and beneficiaries, define the management structure (Foundation Council and Protector if any), and state the foundation's object to operate delivery-only ghost kitchens. The Regulations must include internal governance and distribution rules.
required_dossiers: Original name reservation receipt
Passport copies of the founder, initial Foundation Council members, and Protector
Registered agent engagement letter
Draft Foundation Charter and Regulations in Spanish
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes formal defects or missing consents, rectify the document and re-execute; if any founder's identity is challenged, provide certified translations or apostilled power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Filing and Official Registration of the Foundation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter and Regulations, together with the registered agent's acceptance and proof of payment of government fees, at the Foundation Registry section. The Registry issues the inscribed foundation record (inscripción), completing legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter and Regulations
Registered agent acceptance certificate
Original payment receipt for official filing fees
Cover letter executed by the Panamanian counsel/registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'movimiento de devolución' or defect notice, respond with the corrected wording or supplementary documentation within the Registry-stated period; formal omissions are cured by re-filing the amended page.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Foundation Council, Officers, and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, convene the foundation council to ratify the appointment of officers, adopt corporate resolutions, and issue minutes. Confirm the registered agent's appointment and the registered office in Panama. Establish banking signatories and internal compliance controls.
required_dossiers: Registered foundation record
First Foundation Council meeting minutes (or written consent)
Acceptance letters from appointed officers and Protector
Registered agent service agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer refuses appointment or a conflict arises, pass a supplementary Council resolution replacing the officer and record the change in the foundation records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); Alcaldía/Municipio where the ghost kitchen operates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Tax Identification Number (RUC) with the DGI and register as an employer; obtain fiscal invoice authorization and withholding registration. Apply to the municipality for the Aviso de Operación (business operation notice) for food service premises, including floor plan verification and payment of municipal tax.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
Foundation Council resolution for business commencement
Lease agreement or title of the kitchen premises
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
RUC application and identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or DGI questions address, fire safety, or zoning, submit the lease/addendum, floor plan, and fire-prevention certificate; if the RUC classification is challenged, update the tax activity code to ISIC 5610 food service activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Health, and Environmental Licensing of the Ghost Kitchen
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA); Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the MINSA health operating permit for food preparation and handling; complete building fire-safety inspection and obtain occupancy clearance; assess whether the kitchen triggers an environmental category I registration and, if so, file the digital environmental registration with MiAMBIENTE. Implement grease traps, waste segregation, and ventilation controls.
required_dossiers: Permiso sanitario de funcionamiento application (MINSA)
Fire-safety inspection report from Cuerpo de Bomberos
Building occupancy/structure certificate
Environmental category I registration form (if applicable)
Food handler health certificates for kitchen staff
Waste management plan and grease trap maintenance contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MINSA rejects due to sanitation deficiencies, correct the kitchen layout and apply for reinspection; if MiAMBIENTE requires additional impact analysis, upgrade to a simplified environmental report and supervise the required mitigation measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas e Industrias; Municipality of location for Aviso de Operación; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) for food-service permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal and Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento for Food Service (Ghost/Cloud Kitchen), plus fire-safety occupancy clearance

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Environmental Registration for low-impact food preparation; a full EIA Report is not required unless the kitchen includes high-emission processing, large refrigeration gas volumes, or discharges outside municipal sewer networks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must meet Decreto Ejecutivo No. 131/1997 residual-water discharge limits (pH 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 350 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 220 mg/L, grease/oil below 20 mg/L) and municipal sewer ordinances; kitchen exhaust must control grease and odours, comply with applicable air-quality rules, and refrigeration systems must follow national ozone-depleting substance prohibitions and use proper waste handling

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering extinguishers, hood suppression systems, evacuation routes, and structural load of cooking equipment; workplace health and safety registration with MITRADEL; and employer registration with CSS for kitchen staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; e-Tax online portal: https://etax.gob.pa; DGI informational portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa. Electronic invoicing administration is integrated into the same DGI 'Facturación Electrónica' platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) operating an onshore Ghost Kitchen must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). Procedure: (1) attach the Foundation Charter and Public Registry inscription certificate; (2) file the DGI 'Pre-RUC' online application through e-Tax stating the expected business activity (ISIC 5610 restaurant/mobile food service) and the Panamanian resident agent's address; (3) DGI validates the foundation's existence and legal representative, then assigns a provisional RUC; (4) final RUC is issued after verification of fiscal domicile and acceptance of tax obligations. The same RUC simultaneously covers income tax (ISR) and ITBMS registration. Non-resident founders and beneficiaries are permitted, but a Panamanian resident agent is mandatory for service of process and tax notifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope. The PIF is treated as a separate taxable person, not as a pass-through entity. Only Panamanian-source income is within the tax net; foreign-source income is outside the territorial scope and generally not taxed. A delivery-only cloud kitchen physically operating in Panama derives Panamanian-source income from food sales and delivery services, thus subject to entity-level corporate income tax (flat 25% ISR under the general regime, or simplified progressive rates if annual gross income does not exceed PAB 200,000).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists in Panama. Available statutory elections: (a) the 'Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente' elective simplified regime for taxpayers with annual gross income up to PAB 200,000 (ISR) and up to PAB 36,000 (ITBMS quota payments); (b) exporters may elect the ITBMS input-tax credit/refund recovery mechanism on export transactions; (c) free-zone establishment elections for operations inside Colón Free Zone or Panama Pacifico; (d) territorial-source attribution rules and CFC recharacterisation are mandatory, not elective; consolidation of several Panamanian taxpayers into one ISR return is not permitted — each PIF entity files separately.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panamanian VAT; standard headline rate raised from 7% to 9% by Law 361 of 2024; governed by Código Fiscal Arts. 1057-1102.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general exemption threshold: any natural or legal person habitually carrying on taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama, including a PIF operating a ghost kitchen, must register for RUC and ITBMS before commencing activities (Código Fiscal Art. 1059), regardless of turnover. A reduced simplified-compliance regime is available only where annual gross income is at or below PAB 36,000 (quarterly payment quota system instead of monthly ITBMS filings).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory phased electronic invoicing (DGI Facturación Electrónica): Phase 1 applied to taxpayers with annual billing above PAB 5,000,000 (2020); Phase 2 to those above PAB 1,000,000 (2021); Phase 3 extends to all remaining active RUC holders and new registrants (2022-2024). Invoices must be transmitted in XML via DGI-authorized software through e-factura web-service APIs, digitally signed, and validated by the DGI which returns a 'código de aceptación' (acceptance code). The model is online cycle validation rather than real-time point-of-sale fiscal clearance. Legacy fiscal printers remain permitted for qualifying small taxpayers until full migration deadlines are met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.digital_platform_payout_note: Merchant payouts received from UberEats/DoorDash for deliveries consummated in Panama are domestic ITBMS-taxable receipts at 9%, not export transactions; the platforms may separately be subject to Panama's withholding tax on digital platform services if classified as non-resident digital intermediaries.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies only to: (i) physical export of goods that leave Panamanian territory; (ii) services provided to non-residents for use or enjoyment entirely abroad; and (iii) supplies delivered to a legally recognized free zone (Colón Free Zone, Panama Pacifico) treated as exports. A domestic ghost kitchen selling prepared food through delivery platforms to consumers located in Panama is not eligible for zero-rating: both the food supply and the delivery service are performed and consumed in Panama, attracting the 9% standard ITBMS. Exporter registration in the DGI Registro de Exportadores and customs exit documentation are mandatory to support any 0% claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación - DUA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa) or Panamanian bank statement evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Exporter Register (Registro de Exportadores) inscription and, where applicable, certificate of origin or free-zone movement document
ITBMS export recovery workbook (supporting input VAT credits allocated to exported goods/services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits export zero-rating claims and ITBMS input-credit refunds with strict documentary checks, including customs exit evidence and proof of FX repatriation within 180 days. Non-compliance triggers: surcharge of 15% on unpaid tax (Código Fiscal Art. 749), moratory interest, fines ranging up to 100% of the evaded tax for false records, cancellation of export certificates and exclusion from the Exporters Register, and criminal liability for tax fraud or simulated exports under Law 8 of 2010 and the Código Penal. The ordinary DGI review period is five years, extendable to eight years in cases of omissions or non-filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without a central bank. Banking supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (SBP), established under Decree Law 9 of 1998, while Banco Nacional de Panama serves only as the State's fiscal agent and clearing bank. Monetary policy is effectively displaced by full dollarization under Decree-Law 84 of 1941. The SBP additionally administers the Fintech Innovation Hub and the Regulatory Sandbox created by Law 68 of 2023.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility with zero profit-remittance hurdles. The Balboa is pegged 1:1 to the USD and circulates only as fractional coins; the USD is legal tender for all obligations. Panama has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations since 1946, meaning no exchange controls, no capital-account authorization, no registration for inbound or outbound transfers, and no restrictions on dividends, foundation distributions, royalties, or loan repayments. Panama's constitutional and statutory territorial tax framework (Codigo Fiscal, as amended by Law 76 of 2019) additionally provides that income with foreign source, including the PIF's offshore asset income, falls outside Panamanian tax; the operating SPV's Panamanian-source commercial income is the only layer subject to local taxation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline for export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts, and no central-bank reporting on trade settlement. Ghost-kitchen platform payouts from Uber Eats and DoorDash settle directly in USD into any Panamanian bank account without SBP approval, conversion, or foreign-exchange disclosure. The only operational obligation is the municipal Aviso de Operacion and sanitary licensing of the local operating entity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Restricted and conditional. Law 68 of 2023 establishes a local fintech licensing and e-money framework under the SBP sandbox, but foreign offshore EMIs (UK FCA or EU e-money institutions) are not recognized as regulated deposit-taking institutions in Panama. Using an unlicensed offshore EMI as the treasury anchor would degrade the AML risk rating under SBP Agreement 04-2011 (as amended) and provoke de-risking by Tier 1 banks. A compliant architecture is acceptable: offshore EMI used only as a platform-ecosystem collection/attribution layer for Uber Eats and DoorDash payout aggregation, with a mandatory same-day USD sweep to the Panamanian operational account of the licensed SPV. All ultimate settlement must occur at a domestically licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance is the market standard for first-time corporate account opening: at least one designated signatory and one Foundation Council member (or the resident agent's authorized representative) must attend an in-person interview at the Panama City branch. Remote onboarding is legally possible under the SBP digital-KYC framework only for low-risk existing clients; for a first-time PIF, it is not commercially available. Recommended sequence: resident agent notarizes the foundation charter and council resolutions -> bank pre-screen -> founder and council representative attend branch for signature verification and beneficial-owner interview -> FATCA and CRS self-certifications are executed on site. Realistic onboarding timeline is 3 to 6 weeks versus 1 to 2 weeks for a purely domestic Panamanian S.A. shareholder structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 1 - Beneficial ownership opacity: A Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 has no shareholder register, and nominee council members may obscure the founder's identity; this triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD) under SBP AML/CFT rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the mandatory final beneficial-ownership declaration with the Registro de Beneficiario Final created by Law 254 of 2021; provide certified copies of the foundation charter, internal regulations, and the council resolution identifying founder, beneficiaries, and council members; provide apostilled declarations of source of funds for the statutory founding capital; add professional reference letters from the resident agent and Panamanian counsel; execute FATCA Form W-8BEN-E and the Panama CRS self-certification to close offshore transparency gaps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 2 - Source-of-funds opacity from marketplace settlements: Uber Eats and DoorDash payout flows arrive in aggregated net-commission amounts from foreign payment processors, lacking order-level traceability and any export-invoice foundation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement a dual-entity treasury protocol: the locally licensed SPV (S.A. or S de R.L.) contracts directly with the platforms and receives USD settlements into its operational account; the SPV then pays royalties or management fees to the PIF under a written brand-licence and services agreement; the compliance file includes daily order-level platform reports, settlement statements, inbound MT103 confirmations, intercompany invoices, and a five-year archive under Law 23 of 2015 record-keeping obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 3 - High-risk geopolitical profile: founder or beneficial owner holds residence or citizenship in a FATF grey-listed or sanctioned jurisdiction, or has negative adverse-media exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble: PEP declaration; apostilled police-clearance certificates from every jurisdiction of citizenship or residence; certified CV with a coherent wealth narrative; audited financial statements of the founder's related entities for the past two years; three original bank reference letters dated no more than ninety days before submission; notarized source-of-funds declaration backed by sales deeds, inheritance documents, or dividend vouchers; and a professional introduction letter from the PIF's resident agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 4 - Ultra vires structure: direct operation of a commercial ghost-kitchen business by the PIF violates the passive-asset mandate of Law 25 of 1995 and lacks the local sanitary and municipal licences required for food operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Re-architecture proof: PIF holds 100% of a Panamanian operating SPV; the SPV is the registered holder of the municipal Aviso de Operacion, the MINSA sanitary inspection certificate, and the fire-safety permit; the PIF owns the virtual-brand trademark portfolio and licenses it to the SPV through a written IP licence agreement; the bank file contains the group chart, licence agreement, permits, and SPV board resolutions demonstrating commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 5 - Unsupported mid-cycle capital injections: external investors cannot subscribe equity in a foundation because the PIF issues no shares, so their funding appears as unexplained cash entries without corporate authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Route third-party investor funds as convertible SAFE instruments or shareholder loans into the SPV, not into the PIF; the PIF's own injections are supported by notarized loan agreements with fixed amortisation and an arm's-length SOFR-based spread; each wire is evidenced by SWIFT MT103, board minutes, and updated group capitalization schedules; retain a simplified transfer-pricing file supporting interest and royalty rates paid to the PIF.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital enters via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the selected Panamanian bank's US dollar correspondent (typically JPMorgan Chase New York, Bank of America, or Citibank). Because Panama has no exchange-control legislation, no SBP approval, no purpose-code registration, and no mandatory conversion is required. Recommended wire narratives: (i) founder endowment - 'Aporte de capital a Fundacion de Interes Privado [name]' with the PIF registration number; (ii) shareholder loan - 'Prestamo intercompania' citing the notarized loan agreement date; (iii) brand-royalty collection - 'Regalias por contrato de licencia' citing the licence; (iv) platform settlement sweeps - 'Settlement ghk [brand] - Uber Eats / DoorDash'. The evidentiary file for each injection must include the underlying contract, board resolution, originator bank statement, and the SWIFT message to satisfy SBP AML rule 5.3.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: USD is the functional and settlement currency. Vendor disbursements for packaging, raw-food imports, cloud software, and delivery-locker equipment are executed by SWIFT MT103 from the Tier 1 operational account. For equipment imports exceeding USD 50,000, open an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600), payable at sight in USD, with confirmation through a US correspondent. For Mexican and Colombian ingredient suppliers, settle USD through correspondent clearing or negotiate COP/MXN invoicing with a local bridge intermediary; avoid PayPal and similar wallets as the primary rail due to conversion fees and AML opacity. Platform payouts: Uber Eats settles gross-order balances to the SPV's USD virtual terminal; DoorDash (where operating from a US-domiciled marketplace entity) settles by ACH directly to the same USD account without conversion. A daily automatic sweep, either via local ACH (Camara de Compensacion) or FEDI-style electronic transfer, is mandated to prevent float accumulation in any e-wallet layer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts on MXN/USD and COP/USD with tenors up to 12 months, executed through Banco General or Banistmo derivatives desks to lock ingredient-import costs
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on BRL/USD and CLP/USD for monthly Brazilian and Chilean supply-chain exposures without physical delivery

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) on USD/EUR limited to cases where a EUR-denominated working-capital line is drawn, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement with an SBP-regulated bank counterparty
Zero-Cost Collar option structures on MXN/USD for margin protection on commodity-grade imports
CME-listed micro futures contracts on MXN, BRL, and EUR for short-tenor tactical hedging through an SBP-regulated brokerage affiliate
Plain-vanilla USD interest rate swaps based on SOFR to stabilize debt service on heavy kitchen-equipment financing

Restricted and disqualified: cryptocurrency-denominated hedges (USDT/USDC and similar stablecoins) are treated as high-risk red flags under SBP AML/CFT guidance and will block Tier 1 bank onboarding; they are not permissible treasury instruments for this structure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registry Renewal Payment for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundations Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar year: January 1 through March 31; newly registered foundations must pay the first annual fee within 30 days of inscription
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge per month or fraction of a month after the March 31 statutory deadline; persistent non-payment for two consecutive periods may lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution, with the registered agent subject to sanction for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Re-Confirmation and UBO Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Legal Entity UBO Database / Beneficiary Final Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: within 30 days after the anniversary of foundation registration; any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 calendar days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of B/.500 to B/.5,000 depending on entity size and asset value; registered agent may be temporarily suspended from operating in Panama for repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Panamanian Source Income Tax Return (Issued Only If Ghost Kitchen Conducts Active Operations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, no later than March 15 of the following year; for affected 'Large Taxpayer' designees, deadline is June 1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest of 1% per month on the unpaid tax, plus penalties of 5%–15% of the omitted amount; persistent failure to file can lead to operational closure, seizure of assets, and criminal referral for tax evasion.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent audit is statutorily required for a passive Private Interest Foundation solely by entity type. A compulsory independent audit attaches only when the foundation engages in commercial activity and either is classified as a Large Taxpayer by the DGI or reports gross Panamanian-source annual income of B/.500,000 or more. Below these thresholds, financial statements must be prepared and retained but not filed as audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama Local GAAP (Normas Panameñas de Contabilidad) for non-public entities; IFRS is mandatory for Large Taxpayers and for any legal entity that consolidates subsidiaries or seeks public financing. The foundation must maintain accounting books on an accrual basis as required by the Código Fiscal.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 52 of 2016 and AML/CFT implementing regulations, the registered agent must maintain a certified register of the ultimate beneficial owners and re-confirm the register annually to the DGI's UBO database. Any assignment, transfer, or change in foundation rights, economic interests, or control triggers a mandatory update within 30 calendar days. The annual confirmation must identify each UBO's full legal name, tax residence, and percentage of economic interest; failure to submit constitutes an independent non-compliance offense.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter and Regulations registered at the Public Registry
Register of Beneficiaries and Final Beneficial Owners
Registered Council Resolutions and Minute Book
Register of Legal Representatives and Appointed Officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,200 per year for registered agency, statutory registered office, and secretarial compliance handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – 4,200 for a certified audit when triggered; USD 700 – 1,500 for a non-audit financial review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate tax holiday; Panama applies territorial taxation, exempting foreign-source income. A reduced optional 5% dividend tax regime exists for certain small taxpayers. Private Interest Foundations pay an annual flat franchise tax of USD 350. Expenditures substantiated by invoices are deductible against Panama-source ghost kitchen delivery revenues.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 100 – Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas, filed electronically through the Sede Electrónica de la Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI / MIAM)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; only income sourced in Panama is reportable under the territorial fiscal regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three calendar months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross revenues from delivery-only ghost kitchen operations, including UberEats and DoorDash payout settlements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross delivery platform proceeds attributable to the Panama kitchen and delivery point; do not net delivery commission fees in the revenue line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross revenues earned by the PIF outside Panama, excluded under the territorial tax system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with bank statements and platform seller-resolved location data if any cross-border sales are attributable; PIFs should maintain segregated accounting to avoid audit dispute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: food cost, kitchen rent, staff wages, delivery rider costs, packaging, utilities, and marketing paid through registered bank accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be incurred for Panama-source production, supported by numbered invoices and bank proof; disbursements to related virtual brand companies require arm's-length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (Line 1a minus Line 2) after applying prior-year loss carryforwards limited to five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficiaries have no separate form; the PIF council is responsible for filing and full disclosure. Apportionments of community expenses are disallowed without contract and substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 25% with credit for advance payments and provisional taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned PIFs must make estimated payments on Panama-source income; ensure local payment vouchers reference the RUC of the foundation not the beneficiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend tax reconciliation section applicable only when the PIF resolves to distribute Panama-source profits in the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding on distributions is a final tax. Claim treaty relief only when a double tax agreement applies; otherwise statutory 10% withholding is charged.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 10% of the tax due but not less than USD 50, plus default interest on unpaid tax; prolonged failure triggers DGI administrative closure of the RUC, suspension of the operating licence, and a monetary fine of up to USD 5,000 for non-domiciled taxpayer agents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on distributions of Panama-source profits; a 5% alternative regime may apply in specific small taxpayer cases. Distributions of foreign-source profits are outside Panama's territorial tax and are not withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's limited DTA network (e.g., Korea, Mexico, Portugal, Singapore) requires the beneficial owner to submit to the paying PIF, before the dividend payment is recorded, a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence jurisdiction and the applicable DGI Form requesting reduced withholding. The DGI may require a Beneficial Ownership Statement and proof of substantive activity; excess withholding can be recovered through the 'devolución de pagos indebidos' procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for use of intellectual property in Panama are subject to a 15% statutory withholding; DTA rates typically reduce the rate to 5–10%. Interest paid to non-resident lenders is subject to a 6% statutory rate, except for interest on certain qualifying cross-border loans and licensed bank interest, which may be exempt or treaty-reduced.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama requires a mandatory Local File when the taxpayer's annual gross revenue equals or exceeds PAB/USD 3,000,000; a Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue reaches PAB/USD 50,000,000. Below these thresholds, a simplified TP documentation report is advisable for related-party royalty and brand fees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Panama has adopted economic substance principles aligned with the OECD standards; a Private Interest Foundation conducting a ghost kitchen and virtual brand operation must demonstrate physical premises, local employees, strategic decision-making, and real management of delivery operations in Panama. A PIF that merely holds the brand rights or invoices delivery income without operational substance risks recharacterization and loss of territorial benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional failure to declare cash or platform-generated delivery revenue from UberEats and DoorDash, use of double sets of records, or fabrication of kitchen payroll and food-cost invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fiscal penalty of USD 10,000 to USD 100,000; imprisonment from 4 to 10 years for the responsible taxable persons; compulsory restatement and payment of the omitted 25% ISR plus default interest and a 200% surcharge on the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian law authorises piercing the PIF veil where the foundation is a mere instrumentality; council members, the resident agent, and beneficial owner face joint civil liability, asset embargoes, travel bans, and, upon criminal conviction, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: PIF holds the ghost kitchen licence and payment contracts but has no kitchen premises, no staff, no board minutes, and automatically accepts inflated related-party invoices from an offshore virtual brand company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the foundation's separate existence, assess Panama-source taxation on deemed revenues, apply surcharges up to 200% of tax, cancel the operating licence, and strike the PIF from the registry under Panama's economic substance enforcement rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council are liable for breach of fiduciary duty; Panamanian courts may impose civil restitution, travel bans, and penalty of up to two times the corporate deficiency; criminal sanctions may attach if the arrangement is used as a sham to evade tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling unreported cash from delivery operations, commingling restaurant takings with beneficiary funds, accepting platform payouts into third-party accounts, or using the ghost kitchen to launder illicit cash disguised as food deliveries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's AML Law 23 of 2015 and CNB regulations, fines up to USD 1,000,000 or 200% of the assets involved; freezing and forfeiture of accounts; cancellation of the foundation registration; UAF administrative sanctions and criminal sanctions under the penal code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent may face up to 12 years' imprisonment; travel bans and extended confiscation are routinely applied; the foundation's acts can be retrospectively nullified if vehicles and accounts were used to commit the offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, brand fees, or management charges to a related foreign virtual brand entity without economic justification, comparability analysis, or contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to strip Panamanian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI will make a transfer pricing adjustment, re-characterize the royalty as constructive dividend, assess deficiency plus default interest, add a penalty of 20%–40% of the adjusted tax base, and place the entity on the tax-risk anti-substance list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved the mispriced related-party transaction are personally liable for the underpayment with penalties equal to twice the tax understated; fraudulent documentation elevates liability to criminal tax evasion and travel bans.
